title: EXP-117 - Hello World Part 8 Phase 2 (Designer): GridItems Tile Form FX_ItemsTile, the FX_SignInBtn Collection Refresh Handler on ButtonSignIn2, and One Authorized Regenerate of FX_CustomerPortal, with a Close/Reopen Readback
objective: Build the Designer part of Hello World Part 8 Phase 2 (03:25-04:32) on FX_CustomerPortal (User scope): set GridItems' Tile Form to FX_ItemsTile (EXP-115/EXP-116) and the adjacent tile setting to Always; create the Form event handler FX_SignInBtn (tutorial 'sign in btn') with Response Type Collection Refresh on the secondary collection FX_Items; set ButtonSignIn2's Primary event to FX_SignInBtn; then, with every change saved, click the toolbar Regenerate Form exactly once (operator authorization, 2026-10-18). T1 is a gate that switches the Designer from FX_ItemsTile to FX_CustomerPortal and records the baselines; T2 sets the Grid; T3 creates the handler; T4 wires the button; T5 regenerates; T6 verifies everything after an ordinary close and reopen and writes the final audit. The runtime check (Customer ID 1, sign-in click, tiles) is a separate later experiment (operator decision, 2026-10-18). Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Before browser interaction read AGENTS.md (the repository file, at the start of every task), docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt8.md Phase 2 (lines 114-123), ambiguity items 3 and 6 (lines 270 and 273) and transcript lines 352-362 (03:25-04:32), recipes/components/configure-basic-component.md, recipes/session/session-expiry-and-stale-designer.md, and only the final Outcome (operator) sections of the EXP-116, EXP-114, EXP-095 and EXP-102 records. Read nothing else: no other records and no later Part 8 phases. In a continuation task, AGENTS.md and the current task's part of this record are enough.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-117-hello-world-part-8-phase-2-griditems-tile-form-signin-refresh.md and evidence/EXP-117/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If a session expiry, logout card or sign-in page appears, record it and stop for the operator (EXP-107: the operator signs in manually); do not navigate, type credentials or screenshot a filled sign-in form. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection. Answer any prompt within the same task; never leave a prompt, dialog, menu or unsaved change open across tasks. After any pause, inspect the state read-only before acting and never replay an earlier action. Signed-out session (EXP-116): a server-event error together with a portal tab reading 'Logout Successful' means the session ended; record it and stop for the operator.

Task boundary: do only what the current task instruction lists and stop at its end, even when later steps of this brief remain; report the next step instead of performing it. Turn budget (EXP-109, EXP-111): if a task cannot finish, stop only at a step boundary right after a Save (never with an unsaved change, open list, editor or dialog) and report the next step.

Server-event rule (EXP-103-R2 lesson): if any action raises 'The server event processing returned an error', answer OK once, record it and stop blocked for an operator Designer reload; never try another route, retry, close or reopen after that error. Console-error stop (EXP-110-R2 lesson: a Caption commit can fail silently with HTTP 400 and surface only at the next server event): record the page console error count shown in the browser tool output at the start of each task and after every action in T1 to T6; if it rises after any action, record the action and the counts and stop blocked before any further click (no ellipsis, no Save, no close), leaving the state for the operator. Never read or inspect the console messages themselves. A rise can also come from a client-side Designer script error (EXP-111 T5: an uncaught TypeError at a component selection); the stop rule is the same, and the operator diagnoses the cause from the tool-written console log.

Editing scope: stay in User scope throughout. If an 'Identify Your Editing Scope' dialog appears, confirm it shows User for the signed-in user and accept it unchanged; if it shows any other scope, Cancel it and stop blocked.

Designer gate (T1, read-only except one close and one open): User scope, no dialog open, the open Form clean (Save disabled). If FX_ItemsTile is open, close it once through its Form-tab control (answer No to any save prompt, record its text); open FX_CustomerPortal once through the Form menu recent-forms entry (never Select Form OK). Record: the Components tree (as accepted in EXP-114: GridItems under FlexLayoutHome > Region02: grid with two GridColumns, ButtonSignIn2 under FlexLayoutMain > Region02: signinpage); GridItems' Binding Type and Binding (Secondary Collection Grid, objects2) and every row of its Miscellaneous group with value and, for a list row, its options (open each list view-only and close it without choosing); ButtonSignIn2's Events group (Primary expected blank); the Details Event Handlers tab contents; the Collections entries. Select a component by its Components row, or by its Type cell if the row click does not switch Properties (EXP-113/EXP-114). If the tree differs, Primary is not blank, or no Miscellaneous row is named Tile Form, record it and stop blocked. Record the baseline console error count and screenshots of the tree, GridItems' Miscellaneous group and the Event Handlers tab.

Efficiency rules (operator, 2026-10-16): screenshots only for the decisive states named in this brief; do not re-open saved images unless a decision needs it; one untargeted snapshot per step; read only the named sources; never search or read the worker's own session transcript. Use inline untargeted snapshots; never save snapshots to files and Grep them (EXP-109 ran out of turns that way). Lists (EXP-111 lesson): choose a list option by clicking it; never pick options with arrow keys, Enter or Tab while a list is open, because Tab commits the highlighted item. Stale references (operator ruling, EXP-111): the allowance is one fresh untargeted snapshot per 'Ref not found' error, not one per task. Snapshot size (EXP-114): if an untargeted snapshot is too large to return inline, take targeted snapshots of the needed panel instead (record that); never save snapshots to files.

Field rules (EXP-111, EXP-114): lists: open the list and click the option, then leave the field by clicking the Description row; if the arrow is not exposed, a value-cell double-click may show it; if the planned option is absent, close the list without choosing and stop blocked before the Save. Record the console error count after each action. At most one correction per field. After each performed step exactly one Designer Save, recording its response and the Save state. Answer an OK-only informational prompt with OK and record it verbatim; any other prompt: record it, choose the non-changing answer (No or Cancel) and stop blocked. Leave every other property unchanged.

GridItems (T2): A: Tile Form (Miscellaneous) = FX_ItemsTile (list option click; if the field is a text box, one key-by-key entry and a Description-row click); Save. B: the tile setting is the Miscellaneous row directly below Tile Form whose list offers Always (transcript 'tile and attribute', ambiguity item 3): record its label and options, click Always, Save. If no row below Tile Form offers Always, or more than one candidate row does, record it and stop blocked after A. Two Designer Saves. Screenshots: the Miscellaneous group before each Save; each Save response state.

Handler (T3, EXP-095 route): Details > Event Handlers > New (+) once; in the Event Handler dialog type the name FX_SignInBtn key by key and confirm (record the dialog's fields and buttons first). In the handler's property grid (Event To Handle) record every row, then set Response Type = Collection Refresh (list option click; record the options). Click the Parameters ellipsis once and record the Event Handler Parameters dialog (title, fields, options) with a screenshot before any choice. Set its collection field to the Form's secondary collection FX_Items (an entry naming FX_Items, or objects2 only if the list also shows which collection it is); leave every other field at its default; OK once. If the dialog offers no unambiguous FX_Items entry or asks for anything else, Cancel it and stop blocked before the Save. Record the Parameters summary and the Event Handlers row, then one Designer Save. Screenshots: the Event Handler dialog, the Parameters dialog before the choice, the handler row before the Save, the Save response state.

ButtonSignIn2 (T4): select ButtonSignIn2 (signinpage, not the menu ButtonSignIn); Events > Primary = FX_SignInBtn (list option click); record the value; one Designer Save. Screenshots: the Events group before the Save and the Save response state.

Regenerate (T5, operator-authorized once): with FX_CustomerPortal active and clean (Save disabled) and the T2 to T4 changes saved, click the Designer toolbar Regenerate Form exactly once; record every response or prompt verbatim, the Form open afterwards, the Save state, the console count, and GridItems' Tile Form and tile setting, the handler row and ButtonSignIn2's Primary as displayed. Prompt rule: OK-only informational: OK; a prompt offering to save first or to discard: record it, Cancel, and stop blocked (the Form should already be clean). If an error appears, record it and stop; never repeat Regenerate. Screenshots: before the click, any prompt, after the response.

Readback and audit (T6, one task): close the clean FX_CustomerPortal once through its Form-tab control (answer No to any save prompt, record its text), reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry, and read GridItems' Binding Type, Binding, Tile Form and tile setting, the FX_SignInBtn handler row (Response Type, Parameters summary), ButtonSignIn2's Primary, the Components tree and the Collections entries, from screenshots where values are not exposed as text. Record what the canvas shows in the grid band. Open no dialog or list. Leave FX_CustomerPortal open and clean. Then, in the same task, write the documentation-only final audit into the record: decisive evidence for each acceptance check, the cumulative action audit with exact counts, the worker-written-file inventory, the cleanup inventory and the final state. Screenshots: the reopened Form with the tree; GridItems' Miscellaneous group; the Event Handlers tab; ButtonSignIn2's Events group.

Before every click, use references from the most recent snapshot taken in the current task (not from find output); after any timeout or 'Ref not found', take one fresh untargeted snapshot and use only its references (one per error). ExtJS comboboxes are not <select> elements (EXP-101): open their list and click the option. Coordinates are allowed only once per field for a list arrow that has no reference; record each such click. No canvas placement in this experiment. Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection; never leave a prompt, list, editor or dialog open across tasks. Classify findings as observed only.

Any change to FX_CustomerPortal beyond GridItems' Tile Form and tile setting, the FX_SignInBtn handler, ButtonSignIn2's Primary event and the one Regenerate (no other component, region, property, event, column, variable or collection); any other Form; templates.
Changing the FX_Items IDO or any other global object.
A second Regenerate, or a Regenerate with any Form other than FX_CustomerPortal active or with unsaved changes.
Any other Form, including FX_FlexProbe01; Site Default or Group scope.

Any runtime action in the Web Client.
Check Out, Check In, Undo Check Out or other checkout-management actions; FormSync, deployment; any cache or metadata unload.

Modifying earlier experiment records, AGENTS.md, tutorial sources, recipes, assets or files outside the EXP-117 paths.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Never choose Site Default or Group scope; stay in User scope.
Never create a Form or a template; never run any Form wizard.
Never place, take out, rename, move or resize any component or region; never use mouse dragging; never use Undo; never change a Form property; never define grid columns.

Never set any attribute other than GridItems' Tile Form and tile setting, the FX_SignInBtn handler's name, Response Type and collection parameter, and ButtonSignIn2's Primary event; never create a second handler; never set any other event; never set a Caption or click a Caption ellipsis; never change the Form's collections or variables.
Never create or edit any global object.

Never click Regenerate Form more than once in the whole run, outside T5, with any Form other than FX_CustomerPortal active, or with unsaved changes; never repeat it after an error. Never click Delete Form Definition.
Never edit or save any Form other than FX_CustomerPortal; never perform any runtime action.

Never go beyond the current task instruction; stop at its end even when later brief steps remain.

Never invoke the Designer Save more than twice in T2 or once in each of T3 and T4, or at all in T1, T5 and T6; never retry an uncertain Save; never Save after an error or after the console error count rose; never Save with a dialog open or after the Parameters dialog was cancelled.
Never answer Yes to a prompt that would delete, discard or replace anything; record every prompt verbatim.

Never use direct SQL, application internals or browser JavaScript; never refresh, restart or replace the browser session; re-login only through the worker-preamble session-expiry procedure, at most once per task.
Never claim cross-session durability, database-level durability or replay verification from same-session UI observations.

In T2, Tile Form FX_ItemsTile and the tile setting Always set with their labels and options recorded, two Designer Saves with responses. In T3, the handler FX_SignInBtn created with Response Type Collection Refresh and the FX_Items collection parameter, the Parameters dialog recorded before the choice, one Designer Save with its response. No other component, event, handler, Form or global object changed; FX_ItemsTile unchanged; one Regenerate only; no unload, Delete Form Definition or Select Form OK; no dragging or Undo; no runtime action; no checkout action; User scope only; no task-boundary overrun. The final audit (written in T6) gives decisive evidence for AC-1 to AC-5, the action audit with exact counts (list opens, dialog opens with OK and Cancel, prompts with texts and answers, typed entries and corrections, Designer Saves with responses, Regenerate clicks with responses, Form closes and opens, errors, re-logins), the worker-written-file inventory, the cleanup inventory and the final state.
